title: Upper Deck Seat Track — Local Section Splice Repair in the Galley Bays
abstract: Permanent splice repair for a length of upper deck seat track removed because of corrosion or seat leg damage, restoring the open track profile with a machined splice plate above the floor beam flange.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the seat track load path after a length of track has been removed because of corrosion, fastener hole damage or seat leg pull-out, in the bays under the upper deck galleys and lavatories.
sections.damage_assessment: Establish the extent of the damage after the track section has been lifted, following the applicable removal task. Measure the pit depth over the whole exposed length and record the position of every fastener hole that is elongated or corroded through. Damage that stays inside the allowable limits below may be blended and left. Damage that runs into a splice position, that reaches the floor beam upper flange, or that lies within 100 mm of an existing repair, is outside the scope of this repair. Record the damage position relative to the nearest beam station before you remove any material, because the splice plate layout is set from it.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the damaged length of track by cutting square at two positions at least 120 mm clear of the damage, using the guided saw. Blend the cut edges to a 3 mm radius and do a dye penetrant inspection of both cut faces. Machine the replacement track length from the open section stock and offer it to the gap; the fit must be within the gap tolerance on the repair drawing. Position the splice plate ASH461390-49 above the joint on each side and drill the fastener pattern using the plate as a template, keeping the edge distance given on the drawing. Add the gusset D5170113282765 at the beam station nearest the joint if the joint falls in a bay with no intermediate support. Deburr every hole, apply the surface protection of the standard practice and install the plates dry using rivets AGS611113-6C on the outer rows and tension bolts LN231128K9 into the beam flange positions. Restore the seat leg slot profile across the joint with the profile gauge; the seat leg must pass along the whole repaired length without binding. Seal the joint faces before the floor panels go back.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair is life limited to 20 000 flight cycles from the date of embodiment. Do a repeat detailed visual inspection of the splice plate perimeter and of the seat leg slot every 6 000 flight cycles, and an eddy current inspection of the outer fastener row every 12 000 flight cycles. Any new indication inside the repair boundary makes the repair invalid. Report the repair to Aeralis so that it is recorded against the aircraft, because the upper deck floor is subject to a fleet monitoring programme.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Pitting up to 0.3 mm deep over a length not exceeding 150 mm, no closer than 20 mm to a fastener centre and no closer than 100 mm to a splice position. One damaged length per bay.

issue.reason: Titanium fitting variant published with a wet assembly instruction and a revised fastener specification at the lug positions.
